correctness.rationale: Every entry of the Gram commutator is counted exactly by common predecessor/successor directed edges; this yields K=XWX^T-YWY^T with strictly positive W. The general indefinite-form rank lemma is proved by a bijection to the radical on ker[X,Y]. The incidence kernel is explicitly one-dimensional for nonbipartite graphs and two-dimensional for bipartite graphs; its restricted inverse form is respectively zero or diag(Delta,-Delta). Reversal J gives J K J=-K and exact symmetric positive/negative inertia. The regular special spectrum follows from isometric projection principal angles and the trace-square identity by exact traces. A standalone checker passed 474 finite assertions on multiple graph families; no finite test substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The nonnormality of nonbacktracking dynamics is natural but their ordinary graph-theoretic eigenvalues do not quantify the number of positive/negative selfcommutator directions. This classification applies simultaneously to all finite connected minimum-three simple graphs and exposes an exact nontrivial cancellation hypersurface in bipartite irregular degree data; the integer nullity jumps by two across that boundary. The regular adjacency-angle expression and trace-square identity provide verifiable quantitative consequences. The result is structural rather than a special numerical table or a routine consequence of spectral eigenvalue counts.
